questions.question: Which Rajput ruler defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain?
questions.solution:
• The First Battle of Tarain (1191 CE) was fought between Prithviraj Chauhan (Chahamana dynasty) and Muhammad Ghori.
  • Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori in this battle.
  • However, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE), Ghori returned with a stronger army and defeated Prithviraj Chauhan.

questions.question: Which Pratihara ruler successfully repelled Arab invasions in North-Western India?
questions.solution:
• Nagabhata I was the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty.
  • He defeated the Umayyad Arabs under Junaid in the Battle of Rajasthan around 738 CE.
  • This victory protected north-western India from Arab expansion.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Muhammad of Ghor's battles in India:
1. Muhammad of Ghor defeated Prithviraj Chauhan at the Battle of Chandavar in 1194 AD.
2. In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori.
3. In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Muhammad of Ghor defeated Jayachandra of Gahadavala dynasty at the Battle of Chandavar, not Prithviraj Chauhan.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191).
  • Statement 3 is correct: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

questions.question: In the 11th century, under Mahmud of Ghazni, a small town in ____ became the capital of the vast empire of the Ghaznavids.
questions.solution:
• Mahmud of Ghazni was a Turkish conqueror who attacked India 17 times between 1000 and 1027 AD.
  • In 1018 he plundered the holy city of Mathura and also attacked Kannauj.
  • In 1019 and 1029 he undertook two raids on the Gangetic valley.
  • In 1025 he attacked Somnath (a town on the coast of Kathiawar).

questions.question: In which year Timur's invasion of Delhi took place?
questions.solution:
• Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq of the Tughlaq Dynasty.
  • After the invasion, Timur appointed Khizr Khan as the ruler of Punjab.
  • Khizr Khan later founded the Sayyid Dynasty (1414-1451).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Al-Biruni came into contact with India through Mahmud Ghaznavi in the eleventh century A.D.
Reason (R): Mahmud Ghaznavi invaded India multiple times between 1000 and 1027 AD, during which Al-Biruni accompanied him and studied Indian culture, science, and society.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is correct, but R is incorrect
questions.option_4: A is incorrect, but R is correct
questions.solution:
• Al-Biruni's works like Kitab-ul-Hind and Tahqiq-e-Hind were the outcome of his studies during Mahmud Ghaznavi's campaigns in India.
  • Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

questions.question: When did the Mongol ruler Genghis Khan die?
questions.solution:
• Genghis Khan (original name Temujin) was a Mongolian warrior-ruler, one of the most famous conquerors of history.
  • He consolidated tribes into a unified Mongolia and extended his empire across Asia to the Adriatic Sea.
  • He died in 1227 during his last campaign against the Western Xia.

questions.question: Who among the following was the best-known Chahamana ruler?
questions.solution:
• Prithviraj III (1168-1192) was the best-known Chahamana ruler.
  • He defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191).
  • He was defeated by Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).
  • Vigraharaia II (971-998), Prithviraj I (1090-1110), and Vasudeva (73 BCE-28 BCE) were other rulers of different dynasties.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding provincial architecture in medieval India and choose the correct option:
1. Bengal and Jaunpur developed distinct architectural styles separate from the Delhi Sultanate.
2. Regional styles often blended Islamic structures with local artistic traditions.
3. Provincial styles remained completely uniform across all regions of India.
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Bengal, Jaunpur, Gujarat, Malwa, and the Deccan developed distinct provincial architectural styles under regional sultanates. Example: Bengal used brick and terracotta with curved roofs; Jaunpur featured massive arches with austere ornamentation.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Regional sultanates fused Islamic features (arches, domes, minarets) with local traditions (Hindu temple motifs, lotus patterns). Example: Gujarat mosques incorporated temple-style pillars and carvings.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Provincial styles were not uniform; they varied widely depending on geography, culture, and available materials.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate:
1. The Mamluk (Slave) dynasty was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206.
2. The Khilji dynasty ruled from 1320 to 1414.
3. The Lodi dynasty was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1451 to 1526.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Mamluk (Slave) dynasty was the first dynasty, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Khilji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320, not 1320 to 1414.
  • Statement 3 is correct: The Lodi dynasty was the last dynasty, ruling from 1451 to 1526.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta, who visited India during Delhi Sultanate, originally belonged to which country?
questions.solution:
• Ibn Battuta visited India in 1333 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
  • He was appointed as the qazi (judge) of Delhi.
  • Other notable foreign travelers: Hiuen Tsang (China) - Harshavardhana's court; Al-Beruni (Persia) - came with Mahmud of Ghazni; Francois Bernier (France) - Shahjahan and Aurangzeb's court.

questions.question: In reference to the Delhi Sultanate, what was the 'Group of Forty'?
questions.option_1: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Ilutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziye's killing.
questions.option_2: They were forty military archers who distinguished themselves by their bravery in the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.option_3: They were forty banjara leaders who transferred military supplies in times of war.
questions.option_4: They were forty Rajput nobles who planned a coup to dethrone Qutb ud Din Aibak in 1210.
questions.solution:
• The 'Group of Forty' (Chalisa) in the Delhi Sultanate was a council of powerful Turkish slaves.
  • It was formed by Ilutmish to assist in governance.
  • They took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziye's killing.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Vijayanagara Empire:
1. The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
2. Its first capital was Madurai.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The capital was Hampi, not Madurai.

questions.question: Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate had an influence on the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms?
questions.solution:
• The Iqtadari System was introduced by Shamsuddin Ilutmish (3rd Sultan of Delhi).
  • Under this system, the land of the empire was divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned to soldiers, officers, and nobles.
  • Administrative terms used in Sultanate Period: Dabir (Secretary), Faujdar (Commander of army), Sipahsalar (Commander), Amil (Revenue officer), Diwan (Office: the central secretariat).

questions.question: During the Sultanate of Delhi, the term 'Ulema' was associated with
questions.solution:
• Ulema referred to learned theologians and jurists.
  • Officers in Delhi Sultanate: Amil (Revenue Officer), Barid (Intelligence agents), Khwaja (Accounts Officer), Kotwal (Head of city law and order), Muhatasib (Head of municipality law and order), Muftis (Expounder of law).

questions.question: Who among the following was the daughter of Ilutmish, a ruler of Slave Mamluk dynasty?
questions.solution:
• In 1236, Razia Sultan (Mamluk dynasty) succeeded her father Ilutmish to the Sultanate of Delhi.
  • She sent an expedition against Ranthambore to control the Rajputs.
  • The Mamluk dynasty (1206 to 1290) was founded by Qutbuddin Aibak (Lakh Baksh).

questions.question: Under the Delhi Sultanate, a religious tax was imposed on the wealthy and rich Muslims in India.
questions.solution:
• Zakat was the religious tax imposed on wealthy Muslims.
  • Zakat tax was abolished by Sikander Lodi.
  • Firoz Shah Tughlaq introduced four types of taxes based on the Quran: Kharaj (Land tax), Khams (Tax on booty), Jizya (Imposed on non-Muslims), and Zakat.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding writers of the Delhi Sultanate period:
1. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (1260), written in Persian by Minhaj-us-Siraj.
2. Hasan Nizami wrote Fatwa-i-Jahandari, regarded as the first official history of the Delhi Sultanate.
3. Ziauddin Barani authored Taj-ul-Maasir during the reign of Ilutmish.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (1260) was written in Persian by Minhaj-us-Siraj.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Fatwa-i-Jahandari was written by Ziauddin Barani, not Hasan Nizami.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami, not Ziauddin Barani.

questions.question: Zafar khan was a famous General of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji's generals included: Hizabruddin (Zafar Khan), Almas Beg (Ulugh Khan), Malik Kafur (Taj al-Din Izz al-Dawla), and Nusrat Khan (Malik Nusrat Jalesari).
  • Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Jauna Khan) introduced token currency.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers ruled before Prithviraj Chauhan over Delhi?
questions.solution:
• Ananga Pala Tomar founded Delhi in 1052.
  • An inscription of Vikram Samvat 1383 in the Delhi Museum confirms the founding of Delhi by the Tomars.

questions.question: Who was the author of Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi which is a Persian language chronicle of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi.
  • Amir Khusrau wrote Tughlaq Nama, Nuh Sipihr, and Khazain ul Futuh.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of Delhi sultanate when Ibn Batuta came to India?
questions.solution:
• Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate when Ibn Batuta came to India.
  • Muhammad bin Tughlaq was the Sultan of Delhi from 1324 to 1351 from the Tughlaq Dynasty.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Balban and Bengal:
Statement 1: After the revolt and death of Tughril Beg, Balban appointed his son Bughra Khan as the governor of Bengal.
Statement 2: Balban introduced the practice of Jaziya tax on Hindus as part of his theory of kingship.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• After Nasir-ud-din Mahmud died in 1266, Ghiyasuddin Balban (1266-1287) ascended the throne.
  • He was the first Muslim ruler to formulate the 'theory of Kingship'.
  • Balban introduced the practice of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet of the monarch).
  • Tughril Beg revolted against Balban and declared himself independent ruler of Bengal in 1279.
  • Statement 1 is true: Balban appointed his son Bughra Khan as governor of Bengal.
  • Statement 2 is false: Jaziya tax was not introduced by Balban as part of his kingship theory; he introduced Sijda and Paibos.

questions.question: Which of the following departments of Delhi Sultanate was reorganized by Balban?
questions.solution:
• Balban reorganized Diwan-ii-Atraz (Department of Military).
  • Central Departments of Delhi Sultanate:
    • Diwan-ii-Risalat - Department of Appeals
    • Diwan-ii-Bandagan - Department of Slaves
    • Diwan-ii-Qaza-i-Mamalik - Department of Justice
    • Diwan-ii-Ishtiaq - Department of Pensions
    • Diwan-i-Mustakhraj - Department of Arrears
    • Diwan-ii-Khairat - Department of Charity
    • Diwan-ii-Khai - Department of Agriculture
    • Diwan-i-Wizarat - Head Wazir
    • Diwan-i-Waqoof - Department of Revenue

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Sultan Balban:
Statement 1: Balban was the ninth Sultan of the Slave dynasty who focused more on consolidation of his empire rather than territorial expansion.
Statement 2: Balban is remembered for formulating the 'Din-ii-Ilahi' doctrine during his reign.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Ghiyasuddin Balban (Reigned: 1266-1287) was the ninth sultan of the Slave dynasty of Delhi.
  • He belonged to the famous group of 40 Turkic slaves of Ilutmish.
  • He was the first Muslim ruler to formulate the 'theory of kingship' similar to the divine right of kings.
  • He established the military department 'Diwan-ii-Atz'.
  • Statement 1 is true: He focused on consolidation rather than territorial expansion.
  • Statement 2 is false: 'Din-ii-Ilahi' was formulated by Akbar, not Balban.
